text: During courtship, a male kori bustard inflates its esophagus, displays white underfeathers, and may give a low booming call.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, kori bustard fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/kori-bustard. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A female kori bustard lays eggs in a shallow ground scrape and incubates them. The male does not help rear the chicks.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, kori bustard fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/kori-bustard. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Kori bustards drink with a sucking motion rather than the familiar scoop-and-tip motion of many birds.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, kori bustard fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/kori-bustard. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: American dippers dive into streams to take aquatic insects. A songbird's feeding ground can lie below the water's surface.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone bird inventory; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/birds.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: American white pelicans and other colonial waterbirds nest on Yellowstone's Molly Islands, gathering many nests into a small island setting.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone bird inventory; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/birds.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
